Affiliation:: University of Oklahoma; also affiliated with University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill
Research Domains: Trust, Decision-Making, and Evaluation in Visualization
Techniques Used: Distortion-aware brushing for Multidimensional Projections (MDP): MD density computation, Shared Nearest Neighbors (SNN) similarity, κ-nearest seeds, lens-based relocation, inner convex hull boundary, outer isotropic boundary via offset, centroidal Voronoi tessellation for uniformization, Lloyd’s algorithm, dynamic brush growth, and an erasing mode to refine clusters
MD proximity and closeness metrics to reflect MD relationships in 2D projections and to enable reliable cluster extraction across distorted projections

Visual Stenography: novel sketch-based workflow to externalize user priorities in time-series sketches under noise; FFT-based trend estimation, LOESS-based smoothing for large-scale patterns, persistence diagrams (Topological Data Analysis) for peaks/valleys, Pixel Approximate Entropy (PAE) for noise estimation; iPad-based sketching with Vega-Lite stimuli; data-driven stimulus design with real-world time-series
Subitizing and Fechner’s Law as foundational theories for visualization perception; dual-system theory (System 1 vs System 2) to interpret perceptual biases in projection evaluation
Trust-game methodology for evaluating density-reduction line-chart designs in decision contexts
Comparative evaluation of line-chart density designs (Standard, Aggregated, Trellis, Spiral) using chi-square and t-tests to assess trend identification, prediction, and trust-based decisions

Empirical methods for perceptual biases in DR projection choices, including phase-wise experiments, correlation analyses (Spearman), two-way ANOVA with Tukey’s HSD, and regression modeling with feature analyses
Topological Data Analysis (where applicable), Gaussian Mixture Models with Bayesian Information Criterion (BIC) for cluster structure assessment, and Silhouette scores for cluster quality
Active ranking (Jamieson & Nowak, 2011) to efficiently converge projection rankings from pairwise comparisons
Data & Platforms: - Projections derived from 96 real-world datasets to maximize pattern diversity; 80 projections per condition for the DR projection study

- Visual Stenography: nine real-world time-series datasets (e.g., stock prices, crime rates, weather) used as stimuli; Vega-Lite for stimulus generation; iPad Air with Apple Pencil for sketches; custom web application for sketch capture
- Paper on distortion-aware brushing: simulated and real-world MD datasets; simulated IoT/MDP scenarios; Adversarial robustness toolkit referenced for context in broader literature

- Papers leveraging a mix of platforms and tools: Zoom sessions for experiments, custom stimulus interfaces, Python/R-based analysis stacks; Gaussian Mixture Models (GMM) and Silhouette scoring; LIS (Lloyd’s) for lens uniformization; OSF repositories for supplementary materials
- Visualization and analysis tools cited across the corpus include Vega-Lite, D3.js, scikit-learn (for certain datasets), and standard statistical packages for ANOVA and regression
Application Areas: Data Visualization best practices and perceptual guidance
Visualization-driven education and training in interpretation of high-dimensional data
Interactive visualization tools for clustering and MD-space exploration
Temporal data visualization and sketch-based feature prioritization in noisy time-series
Trust-aware visualization design for decision-making under uncertainty
Dimensionality reduction validation and robustness to projection distortions
Visualization design guidelines informed by cognitive psychology
Key Research Thinking Patterns: Empirical grounding of visualization design in cognitive psychology (dual-system theory, subitizing, Fechner’s Law) to explain perceptual biases and performance
Integrative evaluation across multiple modalities (quantitative experiments, qualitative observations, and user studies) to validate new visualization techniques
Development of robust, scalable interactive methods that explicitly address distortions introduced by dimensionality reduction and projections
Cross-pollination between perception research and practical visualization design (e.g., trust, decision-making, and feature preservation under noise)
Emphasis on reproducibility and transparency through open datasets, supplementary materials, and OSF repositories
Comparison and ablation studies to identify which features and components most strongly drive user performance and trust
Design for generalization across domains: from multi-dimensional projections to time-series sketches to density-reduced line charts
Summary Description: Dr. Ghulam Jilani Quadri is a multi-disciplinary visualization researcher whose work spans perception, interaction, and evaluation in data visualization. Across five co-authored papers, his research consistently addresses how humans perceive and interact with complex representations, from dimensionality-reduction projections to dense temporal data. He advances interactive techniques that improve robustness and interpretability, such as distortion-aware brushing for MD projections and Visual Stenography for sketch-based feature prioritization under noise. He also investigates perceptual phenomena (subitizing, faithfulness vs. visual interestingness) and trust in visualization through empirical studies and design guidelines. Quadri’s work exemplifies a rigorous, theory-informed, and user-centered approach to visualization research, with a strong emphasis on empirical validation, cross-domain applicability, and reproducibility.
